hypothesis: When ES closes a 5m bar through a round-number level (a multiple of STEP points) mid-session, price keeps moving in the crossing direction over the next hour more than random-direction trades taken at the same times with the same brackets.
mechanism: Stop-loss orders cluster just beyond round numbers (Osler 2003). A cross triggers them, and the resulting market orders push price further (a stop cascade). Take-profit orders cluster AT the round number, so the edge, if any, should appear only after a decisive cross, not on a touch.

sources.summary: Osler (2003, JF 58(5)): ~9,700 stop-loss and take-profit orders at one FX dealing bank, 1999-2000. Take-profits cluster at round numbers, stop-losses just beyond them; trends tend to reverse at round numbers and run faster after crossing them. FX, not equity futures.
Donaldson & Kim (1993, JFQA 28(3)): price barriers at round 100s in the DJIA (1974-1990 per a secondary summary; full text not checked).
Ley & Varian (1994), 'Are there psychological barriers in the Dow-Jones index?': the usual sceptical reference, little predictive power from barrier digits. Prior is therefore weak and mixed.

closed_ideas_check: Not on CLOSED_IDEAS.md. Closest closed families are level touches and breaks at VWAP / prior-day high-low / opening-range levels (vwap_rr_*) and profile nodes; all failed, and VWAP 'rejected' about as often as placebo levels. Round numbers are a different level type with an order-placement mechanism specific to the number itself; the closed results still make the prior unfavourable, and the report must say so. Families not in data_spend_ledger for ES.

rules.bars: 5m RTH bars; decision at bar close, fills from the next bar.
rules.levels: L = STEP * n for integers n (STEP in points).
rules.cross: Up-cross on bar k: c_{k-1} < L and c_k >= L + 0.5 (2 ticks through) for some level L; down-cross: c_{k-1} > L and c_k <= L - 0.5. If several levels are crossed in one bar, use the farthest one. No signal from the first bar of the session.
rules.once_per_level: Each level L is traded at most once per session (after its first qualifying cross, later crosses of the same L that day are ignored).
rules.window: bars with ET start 10:00 <= mod <= 14:50 (slots 6..64), so the 60-minute time stop ends before the 15:55 flat.
rules.news_filter: no signal if a scheduled RTH high-impact release time m satisfies bar_end <= m <= bar_end + 5 (a release due before the entry fills). Crosses caused by releases are allowed: the stop-cascade mechanism does not depend on the cause.
rules.entry: market at the next bar's open, side = crossing direction, only when flat with no pending order.
rules.bracket: stop at L - side*STOP_BEYOND (back through the level by STOP_BEYOND points); target at c_k + side*(c_k - stop) i.e. 1:1 about the decision close. Engine snaps prices and measures R from the actual fill.
rules.time_stop: exit at market after 12 completed 5m bars held (60 minutes) without stop or target.
rules.trades_per_session_cap: none beyond one position at a time

walk_forward: fixed: no selection; all three STEP values judged by the frozen dev gate, each needing its grid neighbours positive.
expected_trades_per_session: STEP 25: ~0.5-1.0; STEP 50: ~0.3-0.5; STEP 100: ~0.1-0.25 (STEP 100 may miss the 200-trade dev minimum, which then fails it).
rejection_evidence: Reject if the frozen dev gate fails for every STEP. Report, not gate: whether the effect weakens as the level becomes less 'round' (100 > 50 > 25 is the mechanism's ordering; the reverse ordering counts against it), and the share of trades ending at the time stop.
costs_note: Risk = (c_k - L) + 8 pts, about 8.5-10 pts = $42-50 on MES; base cost ~$3.25 = ~0.07R. Lesson from shock_fade: 4 pt risk gave 0.15R costs.
